collection.description: A net weaver offers young fish to refill the cove, for food: trade, haggle, or decline.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A woman named Rua comes ashore with a canoe full of nets and a basket of tiny live fish swimming in seawater. Rua says the village's cove has been overfished, and that the young fish in her basket, set free in the shallows, will grow and fill the waters again. She asks for food in return. (name1) watches the little fish dart around the basket and has to decide.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) wades out with Rua and tips the basket into the shallows. The tiny fish scatter like thrown pebbles. Months later the fishers swear the cove has never been so full.

o3.name: Outcome C
o3.text: (name1) decides the cove will recover in its own time. Rua nods, and releases a handful of the little fish anyway before she goes. "For the cove," she says.

o2.name: Haggle, the better deal
o2.text: (name1) offers to help Rua repair a torn net while they talk. Rua is so grateful that she empties a second basket into the cove as well, and the shallows flicker silver for days.

o2b.name: Haggle, the worse deal
o2b.text: (name1) haggles hard, and Rua only lets half the basket go, keeping the rest for the next island on her way. The cove fills slowly.

nothing.name: Nothing to trade
nothing.text: Rua sees the village has little food to spare, lets a handful of little fish go in the shallows as a gift, and paddles on.
